subject: Nimble Retail renewal — pricing rebalance and term proposal
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal proposal + short price-hold option

Alex —

Thanks again for the call last week. Based on Nimble's trending usage and the ramp you described, I'm proposing the following as a starting point for the renewal conversation: 

- Term: 12 months (option to extend to 18 months with additional credits)
- Commit: 4.5M token-equivalent monthly average (derived from Q4 usage)
- Price hold: maintain current per-token rate for the first 6 months following renewal
- Credits: one-time credit applied to first invoice (we've penciled 7.5% in the attached term sheet)
- Operational notes: SLA window unchanged; we can include a modest burst buffer for onboarding spikes

I'm attaching a redlineable term sheet (NR_Renewal_TermSheet_v2.pdf) and the usage report we discussed. If Nimble can commit to an 18-month term and a slightly higher floor (5.0M tokens M-avg), we can convert the one-time credit to a pre-paid credit equal to 10% of the first year invoicing and extend the price hold to 9 months.

Can you share your PO timeline? If procurement needs a tighter SOW or a short signature timeline we can jump on a call with finance to align.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal + short price-hold option

Diego —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the term sheet. A few clarifying questions from procurement and finance: 

1) Commitment tiers: The 4.5M token MA is higher than our current monthly average by ~12%. Can you break out the effective per-token price at (a) 4.0M, (b) 4.5M, and (c) 5.0M? We need line items for the procurement package.
2) Credits: If we go the 18-month route and take the 10% pre-paid credit, how does that apply to refunds/credits if usage falls below the committed floor?
3) Timeline: We're working fiscal approvals in the week of Apr 5. Ideally the PO would land by Apr 12 for internal processing. Can you confirm Redwood can hold price and availability until Apr 12 if we agree to the 18-month commit?

Also looping in Maya (finance) for any payment/credit questions. Please include a DocuSign link when the term sheet is finalized — procurement prefers a signed addendum.

Thanks,
Alex Thompson
VP, Engineering Ops | Nimble Retail
alex@nimble-retail.com

Subject: Fwd: Nimble Retail - renewal pricing clarifications

Ben / Monica —

Forwarding Nimble's procurement requests. Key asks: per-token price table at three commit bands, clarification on credit behavior if usage dips, and confirmation we can hold price/availability thru Apr 12 if they sign for an 18-month term.

My read: Nimble wants certainty (PO by Apr 12) and is open to the 18-month incentive. To secure that we'd need to firm the pricing tiers and make the credit non-refundable but applicable as a pre-paid credit that can be consumed against invoices (standard for pre-pay). I want to propose the concession below and get quick approval: 

- Offer: 18-month term, commit floor 5.0M tokens MA, pre-paid credit = 10% of year-1 invoice applied as account credit; credit non-refundable but transferable across Nimble sub-accounts; price hold = 9 months from renewal effective date.
- Contingency: if actual rolling 3-month consumption drops >20% below commit floor, we tier the credit amortization and re-open pricing at renewal; we should include this as a measured underrun clause.

I can present the numbers spelled out in a price table but wanted to align internal approval first. Related attachments: usage_report_Q4.csv.

Thoughts?

Diego

> Attachments: usage_report_Q4.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nimble Retail - renewal pricing clarifications

Diego, Monica —

We can approve the 18-month / 5.0M commit with the 10% pre-paid credit under these conditions: 

1) The pre-paid credit is non-refundable and applied as account credit on invoices; if they downtier below a rolling 3-month average of 4.0M tokens, we amortize the remaining credit over the balance of the term and reserve the right to revisit unit pricing at the next billing quarter.
2) Price hold can be extended to 9 months (from 6) for this concession; outside of the hold period, standard rate applies.
3) Add a small SLA carveout: for enterprise burst above 150% of commit for more than 4 consecutive days, we will allow a temporary burst buffer for onboarding but require notice — this protects capacity.

If those are acceptable I'll sign off and have legal draft the addendum. Also confirm: we can hold availability through Apr 12 conditional on an LOI or signed addendum being in process (we should ask for an LOI by Apr 5).

Deal notes: deal_id = NR-2026-027; margin impact acceptable if they lock 18 months.

Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

Alex / Maya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal approvals, here's a concise counter that reflects what Redwood can commit to if Nimble signs to an 18-month term and confirms a PO/LOI timeline: 

Summary of Redwood's counteroffer (what we'll include in the addendum / DocuSign):
- Term: 18 months (effective on signature)
- Commit floor: 5.0M token-equivalent monthly average
- Pricing tiers (effective per-token rate, ex. credits):
  • 4.0M MA => $0.00112/token
  • 4.5M MA => $0.00106/token
  • 5.0M MA => $0.00099/token
- Pre-paid credit: 10% of year-1 invoicing applied as account credit; non-refundable, transferable to Nimble entities; if rolling 3-month consumption drops >20% below commit floor, remaining credit amortizes over remaining term and pricing may be recalibrated at quarter boundary (simple underrun clause).
- Price hold: 9 months from the renewal effective date
- Burst buffer / SLA: onboarding bursts allowed up to 150% of commit for up to 4 days without surcharge; sustained bursts handled under burst policy in addendum.

Next steps: 
1) If this looks good, sign an LOI (can be a short email) by Apr 5 so we hold price/availability until Apr 12.
2) We'll route the addendum to DocuSign (link will be provided) and begin legal review.
3) Once signed, we'll provision a short enablement/ops kickoff to configure burst thresholds and alerting.

We can jump on a 30-minute call this week to walk the table and make sure the PO timeline is aligned — I'm free Thu 11:00-12:30 or Fri 09:00-11:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Diego Fernandez
